name: Regenerable fixed-bed petroleum cracking
summary: Houdry catalytic cracking, running at Paulsboro by 1936 and Marcus Hook in 1937, passed oil through solid catalyst beds regenerated in turn, so refining never stopped.
description: A refining process passes hydrocarbon feed through a solid catalytic fixed bed and alternates reaction with catalyst regeneration, using multiple beds so feedstock can continue to be processed.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.
why: Car engines needed higher-octane gasoline, and refiners wanted more of it from each barrel than thermal cracking gave.

market.note: The configuration can be supplied or used in economic production, independently of the date and scope of any first offer.

evidence.supports: Reports that a Socony-Vacuum catalytic cracking unit went into operation in 1936 at Paulsboro, New Jersey.
Dates the Paulsboro thermal-unit conversion to April 1936, describes it as semi-works, and discusses regeneration improvements; conversion month is not treated as the operating date.
Describes the 1936 Houdry process as continuously fed multiple fixed-bed reactors alternating cracking and catalyst regeneration.

date.label: By 1936
date.basis: C&EN reports operation in 1936; the 1936 bound is one-sided, and ACS dates conversion, not necessarily startup, to April.

events.statement: A Houdry catalytic-cracking unit was operating at Socony-Vacuum’s Paulsboro refinery by 1936.
events.scope: Houdry catalytic cracking in a converted refinery unit using multiple fixed beds with alternating conversion and catalyst regeneration.
events.caveats: ACS describes the April 1936 conversion as semi-works, whereas Penn State describes 1936 as commercial. The 1936 operating year does not establish the precise operating day, first sale, or global priority. A 1933 Houdry unit existed before later regeneration improvements, and its exact configuration is not established here.

events.statement: In March 1937 Sun Oil put its commercial Houdry catalytic-cracking unit into operation at Marcus Hook.
events.scope: Houdry catalytic cracking using multiple fixed beds with alternating conversion and catalyst regeneration.
events.population: Sun Oil refinery operators at Marcus Hook
events.caveats: Earlier McAfee aluminium-chloride batch catalytic cracking existed. The Paulsboro unit was operating by 1936 and is described by ACS as semi-works, while other sources use commercial terminology. This event fixes the larger Marcus Hook plant’s operational month only; it does not establish the first sale of a catalyst or fuel.

evidence.supports: ACS identifies Sun’s Marcus Hook unit as fully commercial and dates its operation to March 1937; the source separately describes catalyst regeneration.
Describes continuously fed multiple fixed-bed reactors alternating cracking with catalyst-regeneration cycles.
